## Plan

Follow-up to tech-119 (D-33): the Playwright suite signs in through
Keycloak's own form with a real password, which this project's agents may not
type — so every E2E run costs a human today, and so does the stand's
`scripts/keycloak-seed.sh`. This task removes both.

Size L — the implementation plan goes to `plan-backend.md` / `plan-frontend.md`
at stages 4 and 6; here only the route:

spec.md (scope from the queue line: no password in the run, seed from
AppHost) → review-requirements → gate-1 → dev-backend (stand-only Keycloak
client with impersonation, kept out of the production realm import; AppHost
runs the seed) → QA backend → dev-frontend (`src/frontend/e2e`: the suite
obtains its session through that client, admin API calls move to it,
`E2E_PASSWORD` disappears) → QA frontend + a real E2E run → review → gate-3 →
local squash into main.

Stage 3 is skipped — not a single screen changes, so UX design has no
subject and `gate-2` does not appear here. An ADR is expected on the
stand-only impersonation client: it is a decision that outlives the task.

## Decisions

- D-1 (human 2026-09-12, form) **Size L, not the `size:M` of the queue
  line.** Threshold "the authentication/authorization rules or the handling of
  secrets change" fires: a confidential client able to obtain a session as any
  user appears in realm `mustask`, and it must never reach the production realm
  import.
- D-2 (human 2026-09-12, form) **Scope is exactly the queue line** — a run
  without a password and the seed started by AppHost. The E2E question of
  tech-119 D-32 stays: the agent keeps asking the human whether to run E2E in
  a given task. Making E2E a mandatory pre-review step, and raising a stand in
  CI, were both rejected (CI itself does not exist yet — `tech-060`).
- D-3 (human 2026-09-12, form, OQ-1) **The suite signs in as a dedicated
  fixture user**, not as the human's own `mustask` administrator: a human's manual
  `keycloak-seed.sh` run and the automatic seed must not fight over one
  account, and the Keycloak event log must tell a suite run apart from a live
  administrator. The identity still has to satisfy R-7 — specs 6 and 11 need
  administrator rights and the username the suite signs out by.
- D-4 (human 2026-09-12, form, OQ-2) **AppHost seeds only what E2E needs** —
  the stand-only client and the fixture user. The human-facing accounts
  (`mustask`, `partneradmin`, `inspector`, `operator`) stay with
  `scripts/keycloak-seed.sh` and passwords the human chooses. R-5's fact
  (the script refuses to run without both `MUSTASK_PASSWORD` and
  `PARTNER_PASSWORD`) therefore does not block BR-6: the automatic seed is a
  separate path, not a call into that script.
- D-5 (human 2026-09-12, form, R-2 blocker) **The client's secret is
  generated by AppHost at stand start and handed to the suite through a
  gitignored stand file** — no fourth mandatory human-set secret on a fresh
  clone, and no human moving a value into the run's environment. Accepted
  knowingly: the right to impersonate lies in plaintext on the developer's
  disk and is readable by the agent; what keeps it safe is that it exists
  only in a stand realm (BR-2). A human-set user secret was rejected as the
  manual step this task removes; a public client with no credential was
  rejected outright — Keycloak binds all interfaces (R-8).
- D-6 (human 2026-09-12, form, OQ-3) **The agent may stop and start the
  Keycloak container of the stand it started itself.** Two conditions, both
  acceptance criteria: the container is resolved unambiguously (OQ-4's
  narrowing is required, not optional — `docker ps -a --filter name=keycloak`
  takes the first match today), and it is restored even when a run is
  aborted (R-12).
- D-7 (human 2026-09-12, chat "да", OQ-5) **The password sign-in path is
  removed, not kept as a fallback.** After impersonation a human's own run
  takes the same path the agent's does, so a second sign-in route would be
  one nobody exercises. `E2E_PASSWORD` disappears from the suite,
  `src/frontend/AGENTS.md` and `docs/runbooks/stand.md`. Spec 3 keeps
  driving Keycloak's real form with its deliberately wrong literal — that is
  not a credential.

- D-8 (human 2026-09-14, chat "делай А") **The stand's own access-token
  lifespan is set once by AppHost, not by the specs.** Specs 6, 9 and 11 need
  a short-lived token to observe a renewal without waiting 14 minutes each;
  writing that setting needs realm-configuration rights, which the stand-only
  client deliberately does not have. Rather than widen a client that can
  already impersonate anybody, AppHost sets the lifespan at stand start with
  the Keycloak administrator credentials it already holds. The three specs
  then stop writing the realm at all and stop skipping. Accepted cost: the
  stand's access token lives ~2 minutes instead of the production 15, so the
  panel renews often during manual work — a deviation to be written into the
  runbook. Granting the client `view-realm`/`manage-realm` was rejected as
  widening rights for test speed rather than for what is being tested; the
  full `realm-admin` composite was rejected outright.

- D-9 (human 2026-09-15, chat "да, делай e2e", tech-119 D-32) **This task
  does its E2E run.** The question the D-32 rule puts at the last QA stage
  before code review was asked and answered yes — with the note that here it
  is not an extra: the suite's own unattended run is what this task delivers,
  so without it there is nothing to accept.

- 2026-09-15 [orchestrator] **Defect found by the human at gate-3, fixed:
  the suite was not actually safe to start on a cold stand.** Their run lost
  specs 1 and 2 on 30s timeouts; the screenshot showed the panel's
  «Сервис аутентификации недоступен», i.e. `authError=idp_unavailable` —
  the sign-in never began. Cause: `/api/session/login` refuses to issue a
  challenge while `RealmReadiness.Current.IsReady` is false
  (`SessionEndpoints.cs:76`), and `Mustask.Api` learns the realm is up only from
  `RealmReadinessMonitor` — 30s `CheckInterval`, readiness *latches* once
  reached. On a warm stand the API latched long ago and `docker stop`/`start`
  cannot unlatch it, which is why three QA runs and my own re-runs all passed;
  on a cold one the gap is up to 30s and `auth.ts`'s sign-in timeout is also
  30s, so it was a coin flip. The global setup checked `Mustask.Api` only through
  `/alive`, which is deliberately tag-limited to `live` and documented as not
  seeing realm readiness (`RealmReadinessHealthCheck.cs`); its realm and
  credential checks are made from Node and go green as soon as Keycloak
  answers — nobody asked the API. Fix: `e2e/support/apiReadiness.ts` polls
  `/health` (up to 120s, and says in the run log when it had to wait) before
  any spec runs. `/health`'s `keycloak-realm` check and the login endpoint
  read the *same* singleton `RealmReadiness` (`Program.cs:160`), so the gate
  waits on exactly the state that decides the failure — not on a proxy.
  Evidence: reproduced live on a cold stand (artifacts kept this time, not
  destroyed by a re-run); new `src/test/e2eApiReadinessGate.test.ts` proven
  red against the old behaviour («expected 1 to be 3» — it proceeded after
  the first answer) and green with the gate. **Not a new requirement and
  `gate-1` is not reset**: US-1/US-4's criteria already say the suite runs
  unattended — this makes them hold on a cold stand.
  **Live proof, on the failing precondition itself:** a cold stand measured
  `/health` = `Unhealthy` one second before the run started — the exact
  state in which the old suite lost specs 1 and 2 — and the full suite then
  passed **13/0/0 (4.8m)**, specs 5 and 6 included (`E2E_ALLOW_DOCKER=1`).
  Three earlier cold cycles had all landed on the lucky side (the API latched
  before the stand file was written) and proved nothing; this one did not
- 2026-09-15 [human] **ADR-0023 accepted** (form at gate-3) — the stand-only
  impersonation client is now a recorded decision, status flipped in the ADR
  and its index. gate-3 itself is not given yet: the human is checking the

## Notes

Inheritance from tech-119 for this task:

- `status.md` D-33 fixed the approach: a stand-only confidential client with
  the impersonation role obtains an SSO cookie for a fixture user, after which
  the panel walks its own ordinary login flow; the suite's admin API calls
  move to that same client; AppHost runs the seed.
- `qa.md` (§ E2E) and `src/frontend/AGENTS.md` (§ E2E test suite) describe
  what the run needs today, including which specs skip without
  `E2E_KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `E2E_ALLOW_DOCKER=1` — those two
  variables are part of the same problem.
- `design.md` §7.3 item 12 is deliberately not in the suite: the harness
  cannot restart `Mustask.Api` under Aspire. If this task gains that ability, the
  item can come back.
